quotes.text: Quantum computing merely accelerates the need for cryptographic agility that's already apparent from past algorithm deprecations and protocol shifts.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes the quantum threat as one instance of a recurring algorithm-transition problem.

quotes.text: Without continuous discovery, crypto agility is a slogan. You can't be agile if you don't know where the crypto is.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Makes cryptographic inventory the concrete prerequisite for agility.

quotes.text: Cryptographic agility isn't a technical capability you can buy. It's an organizational discipline you have to build.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear thesis that the transition is an organizational, not a product, problem.

quotes.text: Don't treat the post-quantum migration as a project with an end date, treat crypto agility as a permanent operational discipline.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Actionable recommendation on how to frame the PQC program.

quotes.text: Starting with remediation before you have governance and inventory is like performing surgery before you've diagnosed the patient.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable analogy for the correct sequencing of the migration.

takeaways: Adversaries are already harvesting encrypted traffic, so data that must stay confidential for decades is at risk today, long before a quantum computer exists.
The real weakness is rigid, hard-coded cryptography; modularity, API abstraction, policy separation and hybrid key exchange make algorithm changes survivable.
Start with governance and a continuous cryptographic inventory, then use what Microsoft already ships (SymCrypt, AD CS ML-DSA, Key Vault previews, Edge defaults) for phased PQC adoption.
hook: Quantum computers will break RSA and ECC, and attackers are already storing your encrypted traffic to decrypt it later. This episode is for security architects and Microsoft 365 and Azure administrators who need a realistic post-quantum plan. You will learn why cryptographic agility, not a single algorithm choice, decides whether your organization survives the transition.
